phase_1: paraelectric, H on short O-H-O bridge dynamically disordered
direction_evidence: K3D(SO4)2 orders to the antiferroelectric phase on cooling while K3H(SO4)2 stays paraelectric -> D expands the low-T ordered field.
conditions: ambient pressure, cooling from room temperature; experimental result cited in a path-integral MD paper
magnitude: Tc(D)=84 K; no transition for H
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: H/D order-disorder in short H-bond, tunnelling suppresses ordering in H
quote: its deuterium-substituted counterpart, K3D(SO4)2 (DKHS), undergoes a phase transition to an antiferroelectric state at a critical temperature of 84 K
note: Experimental fact quoted from a computational paper; primary experimental reference not seen.

direction_evidence: Transition near 85.5 K exists for K3D(SO4)2 but not for K3H(SO4)2 -> D favours the low-T phase.
conditions: single-crystal neutron diffraction and INS, cryogenic to room temperature
magnitude: Tc(D) about 85.5 K; absent for H
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: split-wavefunction/tunnelling picture, isostructural quantum transition
quote: the phase transition observed for K(3)D(SO(4))(2) at T(c) ≈ 85.5 K, which does not exist for K(3)H(SO(4))(2)
note: Neutron diffraction finds no resolvable structural change in the average structure, so the two phases differ in H/D wavefunction rather than symmetry.

direction_evidence: AF ordering temperature is about 50 K for H and 168 K for D -> D raises the temperature below which the AF phase exists.
conditions: low-T absorbance spectra, ambient pressure
magnitude: AF ordering below 50 K (H) vs 168 K (D)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: phonon-assisted proton tunnelling in H, deuteron hopping in D
quote: difference in the antiferro-electric (AF) ordering mechanisms below 50 and 168 K in Cs3H(SeO4)2 and Cs3D(SeO4)2, respectively

direction_evidence: Source states the high-T ferroelastic-superionic transition shows a negative isotope effect (lower Ti on deuteration) -> D favours the high-T superionic phase.
conditions: above room temperature, ambient pressure
magnitude: Ti lowered on deuteration (value not in abstract)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: superionic transition from destruction and reconstruction of H-bonds
quote: negative isotope effect in which lowering of the transition temperature is seen by the deuteration
note: Source says 'most cases' of the M3XY2 family, example given Cs3H(SeO4)2 to Cs3D(SeO4)2.

direction_evidence: Cs3D(SO4)2 shows a superionic transition near 422 K while Cs3H(SO4)2 shows none from 350 to 490 K -> D favours the high-T superionic phase.
conditions: DSC, dielectric constant and conductivity, 350 to 470 K
magnitude: Ti(D) about 422 K; none for H up to 490 K
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: superionic phase, H-bond network reconstruction
quote: no protonated compounds TCHS exhibited the phase transition in the temperature region from 350K to 490K
note: Absence of the H transition could also be a decomposition limit near 490 K; direction inferred from the negative-isotope-effect trend in the same abstract.

direction_evidence: TlD2PO4 goes directly para-antiferroelectric at 353 K whereas TlH2PO4 reaches the antiferroelectric phase only at 229.5 K via an intermediate ferroelastic phase -> D expands the AF phase field.
conditions: ambient pressure, neutron diffraction; H value from separate paper (Acta Cryst B 2006, 10.1107/s0108768106018222)
magnitude: AF onset: 353 K (D) vs 229.5 K (H); H also has a transition at 357 K to the ferroelastic phase
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: ordering of inequivalent H(D) atoms in O-H...O bonds
quote: The para-antiferroelectric transition (T_c^d = 353 K) of TlD2PO4 is analysed from a structural point of view
note: Phase sequences differ between H and D, so this is an isotope-dependent phase sequence, not a simple shift.

direction_evidence: Ttr(KOD)=253.1 K > Ttr(KOH)=226.7 K for the transition into the low-T antiferroelectric phase -> D favours the low-T ordered phase.
conditions: heat capacity 17 to 342 K, ambient pressure
magnitude: +26.4 K on deuteration (226.7 vs 253.1 K)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: tunnelling of OH/OD between two minima of a double-well
note: Abstract text taken from the Crossref record. Later PIMD paper 10.1021/acs.jpcc.1c06953 states the same direction.

direction_evidence: NaOD undergoes a first-order transition into the AFE phase that is absent in NaOH -> D favours the low-T AFE phase.
conditions: ambient pressure, cooling; applied pressure drives the same transition
magnitude: transition present for D, absent for H
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: zero-point fluctuations stretch weak H-bonds, quantum paraelectric
quote: NaOD undergoes a first-order transition, which is absent in NaOH.
note: Experimental observation quoted in a path-integral paper; applied pressure has the same stabilising effect on the AFE phase.

direction_evidence: Tc increases on deuteration (KD2PO4 higher than KH2PO4) for the para to ferroelectric transition -> D favours the low-T ferroelectric phase.
conditions: ambient pressure, neutron diffraction on KDP and DKDP
magnitude: deuteration at constant O...O distance still raises Tc by about 40 K (total shift larger, value not in abstract)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: order-disorder ferroelectric, proton tunnelling plus geometric effect
quote: deuteration at constant 2R still gives rise to an increase in T c by about 40 K
note: Abstract also says the large increase in Tc on deuteration is partly geometric (longer O...O).

direction_evidence: Experimentally the isotope effect on Tc collapses under high pressure, so at high pressure H and D behave the same (at ambient D favours the ferroelectric phase).
conditions: high pressure, KDP vs DKDP
magnitude: isotope effect on Tc collapses at high pressure (no value in abstract)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: quantum paraelectric phase at high pressure
quote: the experimentally observed collapse of the isotope effect under pressure
note: Computational paper citing experiment. Related experimental paper (Endo et al., PubMed 11801070) has no DOI in Bond: Tc of both KDP and DKDP vanish above critical pressures.

direction_evidence: High-T transition occurs at 133 C in NH4H2PO4 and 141.5 C in ND4D2PO4 -> D raises the temperature at which the room-T phase is left, so D favours the low-T phase.
conditions: conductivity and dielectric measurements, ambient pressure
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: no: attributed to ammonium ion motional effects
quote: The corresponding transition in ND4D2PO4 observed here for the first time takes place at 141.5 °C.
note: H value (133 C) from the same abstract. Both ND4 and OD deuterated, so not a pure O-H effect.

direction_evidence: P21nm to Pnnm transition at 9.0 GPa for AlOOH and 13.4 GPa for AlOOD -> D raises the pressure at which phase_1 is left.
conditions: room temperature, high-pressure neutron diffraction
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: phase_2 is H-disordered, mass effect on tunnelling and zero-point vibration
source_location: full text, section 'D/H Isotope effect on phase transition' (Europe PMC PMC6195538)
quote: the transition pressure was found to be 13.4 GPa in the case of δ-AlOOD, which is 4.4 GPa higher than that of δ-AlOOH.
note: Abstract only says significant isotope effect on transition pressure; numbers from full text.

direction_evidence: H becomes symmetric at 18.1 GPa; D distribution still bimodal at 17.4 GPa, the highest pressure reached -> D shifts symmetrisation to higher pressure, favouring the disordered phase.
conditions: room temperature, high-pressure neutron diffraction
magnitude: AlOOH 18.1 GPa; AlOOD above 17.4 GPa (not observed)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: H-bond symmetrisation after disorder
source_location: full text, section 'D/H Isotope effect on phase transition'
quote: the distribution remained bimodal and did not merge into a single peak in the case of δ-AlOOD
note: Lower bound only for D.

direction_evidence: FeOOH goes P21nm to Pnnm at 17.90 GPa while FeOOD stays asymmetric over the same range -> D favours P21nm.
conditions: room temperature, powder neutron diffraction above 20 GPa
magnitude: H: 17.90 GPa; D: not reached by about 20 GPa
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: phase_2 has disordered H-bonds
quote: while ε-FeOOD remained asymmetric

direction_evidence: Spin-reorientation observed at the same 8 GPa in both FeOOH and FeOOD -> no isotope shift.
conditions: room temperature, high pressure neutron diffraction
magnitude: none (8 GPa both)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: no: magnetic transition
quote: The magnetic transition was observed at 8 GPa in both ε-FeOOH and ε-FeOOD.
note: Negative finding for the magnetic transition; the structural P21nm to Pnnm transition does shift (previous row).

direction_evidence: Authors found no significant difference between Ca(OH)2 and Ca(OD)2 in the phase-transition pressure.
conditions: DAC, room temperature, IR and synchrotron XRD up to 25 GPa, He or methanol-ethanol medium
magnitude: none; OH(OD) IR splitting at 6-7 GPa for single crystals
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: unclear: H-bond geometry change accompanies the transition
source_location: companion Goldschmidt 2011 conference abstract p.1078 (journal abstract not retrievable; DOI is that of the full paper, title seen on Crossref and OpenAlex)
quote: No significant difference suggesting the isotope effect was found in the phase transition pressure.
note: Hydrostaticity strongly affects the transition, which may mask a small isotope shift.

compound: water ice (ice VII to symmetric-bond phase)
direction_evidence: Transition at 60 GPa in H2O ice and 70 GPa in D2O ice -> D raises the pressure at which ice VII is left.
conditions: 85 to 300 K, up to 210 GPa, IR reflectance
magnitude: +10 GPa (60 vs 70 GPa)
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: H-bond symmetrisation of proton-disordered ice
quote: a phase transition at 60 gigapascals in H2O ice (70 gigapascals in D2O ice)

direction_evidence: Ih to XI onset 58.9 K (H2O) vs 63.7 K (D2O), XI to Ih 73.4 K vs 78.2 K -> D raises both temperatures, expanding ice XI.
conditions: dielectric constant, ambient pressure; triple point Ih/II/XI at 0.07 GPa, 73.4 K (H2O) and 0.08 GPa, 78.2 K (D2O)
magnitude: +4.8 K on cooling onset, +4.8 K on heating
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: proton ordering transition
quote: For D2O, TIh-XI = 63.7 K and TXI-Ih = 78.2 K.
note: H2O values from same abstract: TIh-XI = 58.9 K and TXI-Ih = 73.4 K.

direction_evidence: Ice II to Ic enthalpy is +40 J/mol for H2O but -140 J/mol for D2O, so ice II is relatively less stable in D2O than in H2O (enthalpy only, ambient pressure).
conditions: calorimetry at ambient pressure after recovery
magnitude: transition enthalpy +40 vs -140 J/mol
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: unclear: zero-point energy effect
quote: While the ice II to ice Ic transition is endothermic for H2O, it is exothermic for D2O samples.
note: Enthalpy sign change is not a direct measurement of free-energy ordering or of a shifted phase boundary.

direction_evidence: Abstract says H/D substitution shifts the order-disorder transition by 4-6 K but gives no sign.
conditions: HCl-doped samples, ambient pressure
magnitude: 4-6 K shift
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: hydrogen order-disorder
quote: H/D substitution was found to slow down the dipolar dynamics up to about 30-fold and shifts the order-disorder transition by 4-6 K
note: Also: D2O samples reach a lower degree of order than H2O at the same cooling rate (kinetic effect).

direction_evidence: Replacing H by D raises the low-T Pmcn to P21cn transition by about 27 K (155 K for D) -> D expands the low-T ordered phase.
conditions: neutron powder diffraction 1.6 to 505 K, ambient pressure
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: proton ordering
quote: Replacing H by D causes the low temperature transition point to be increased by ~27 K

direction_evidence: High-T Cmcm to Pmcn transition (271 K in D) is unchanged within about 2 K relative to the hydrogenous sample.
conditions: neutron powder diffraction 1.6 to 505 K
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: partly proton order-disorder but displacive component dominates
quote: The transition point of the hightemperature transition remains the same within ± ~2 K.
note: Negative finding on the 271 K transition.

phase_2: deuterated-type structure (long Cu-O(8) bond, Jahn-Teller switch)
direction_evidence: Deuteration produces a structural change (long Cu-O bond switches direction); the H salt is the 'anomalous form' that persists, enthalpy difference 0.17 kJ/mol at 295.8 K.
conditions: 15 K neutron diffraction; deuterated salt held in metastable H-type state via 500 bar at about 303 K
magnitude: enthalpy difference 0.17(2) kJ/mol
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: no: hydrogen-bond strength change, not proton disorder
quote: the origin of the structural phase change that is known to occur upon deuteration
note: Which isotopologue prefers which form follows the abstract wording about stabilising the hydrogenous salt in the anomalous form.

direction_evidence: Structure switches abruptly from H-type to D-type at about 50% deuteration at 293 K -> D (at high fraction) selects the other structure.
conditions: EPR vs degree of deuteration at 293 K, neutron diffraction at 15 K
magnitude: switch near 50% D
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: no: H-bond driven Jahn-Teller distortion
quote: the structure changes quite abruptly from that of the pure hydrogenous salt to that of the fully deuterated salt at approximately 50% deuteration

direction_evidence: Tc of KH3(SeO3)2 is 211 K; a web-search summary of the NMR literature gives Tc about 302 K for KD3(SeO3)2 -> D raises Tc (unverified secondary value).
conditions: ambient pressure, NMR and Brillouin studies
magnitude: 211 K (H) vs about 302 K (D); D value from search summary, 296 K also reported
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: ordering of O(2)-H-O(2) hydrogens
source_location: title only seen (paper compares KH3(SeO3)2 and KD3(SeO3)2); no abstract available
note: LOW CONFIDENCE: numbers come from a WebSearch summary of a Springer NMR paper, not a verbatim source; 211 K for H confirmed in the abstract of 10.1016/j.chphi.2026.101123.

compound: general H-bonded ionic and molecular crystals (review)
direction_evidence: Review states some H-containing crystals transform only when deuterated (D induces the low-T transition) but names no specific phase pair in the abstract.
conditions: low-temperature calorimetry
proton_disorder_or_tunnelling: yes: tunnelling of protons and deuterons
quote: Some of the molecular and ionic crystals containing hydrogen undergo phase transitions only when they are deuterated.
note: Pointer to the literature (calorimetry of deuteration-induced transitions); not a specific compound row.
